prompt_text: I need a personal injury lawyer in Phoenix after a car accident. Which specific law firms should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Phoenix for a car accident case?
answer_verbatim:
I can help — quick question first: do you want a big national firm with lots of resources, or a smaller local firm that’ll give you more personal attention? Also, what part of Phoenix (ZIP or neighborhood) are you in, and how serious are your injuries? That will help me tailor specific firm suggestions.

Note: I don’t have live web access in this chat, so I can’t pull an up‑to‑the‑minute list. If you want, give me your ZIP and preference and I’ll produce a short prioritized list of firms to call based on the latest public ranking sources and the criteria below. Meanwhile, here’s immediately useful guidance — who to call, what to look for, and exactly what to ask.

Who to call (three types — call at least one of each)
- Large regional/national personal-injury firms with local Phoenix offices: they bring resources for medical experts and litigation. Good if injuries are severe or liability is contested.
- Established Phoenix boutique personal-injury/trial firms: often more hands‑on, know Arizona law and courts, and may be quicker to communicate.
- Highly rated solo/small-firm trial attorneys: choose if you want close personal contact and an attorney who will try your case if needed.

How to find specific firms fast
- Arizona Bar Lawyer Referral Service (azbar.org) for screened attorneys.
- Search “personal injury attorney Phoenix” and filter by: Super Lawyers, Avvo/Justia ratings, Martindale‑Hubbell AV ratings, and client reviews.
- Look for membership in Million Dollar Advocates Forum or significant verdict/settlement reports (if available).

What to prioritize when choosing a firm
- Regularly handles car-accident cases and has experience with injuries like yours.
- Trial experience and a record of taking cases to verdict (not just settlements).
- Contingency fee agreement (no fee unless you recover) and clear fee structure.
- Good client communication: who will be your direct contact?
- Local courtroom experience (Maricopa County) and relationships with medical experts.
- Positive client reviews and peer recognition (Super Lawyers, AV Preeminent).

Exact questions to ask on the phone (use these with every firm you call)
1. Do you handle car-accident personal injury cases in Phoenix regularly? (Yes/No)
2. Who will handle my case day-to-day — an attorney or a paralegal? Will I meet the attorney in person?
3. Do you take cases on contingency? What is your fee percentage and are there other costs I might owe up front?
4. Have you tried similar cases to verdict in Maricopa County? Can you share results or references?
5. What is your approach to cases like mine — settlement vs trial? What kind of recovery do you expect?
6. How long do you think a case like mine typically takes to resolve?
7. Will you obtain medical records and bills, and coordinate care if I don’t have a treating provider yet?
8. Do you have language capabilities (if you need Spanish or another language)?

What to bring to your free consult (or send by email before the call)
- Police report number (if there is one)
- Photos of the vehicles and injuries
- Medical records and bills or the name/location where you were treated
- Insurance information for all parties
- Names/contact of witnesses
- A short timeline of the crash and injuries

Safety and timing
- Seek medical care immediately if you haven’t already — that’s critical to both health and your claim.
- Arizona has a statute of limitations (typically 2 years for personal injury); don’t delay contacting an attorney.

If you want specific firm names and numbers right now, tell me:
- Your ZIP/neighborhood in Phoenix, and
- Preference for large vs boutique firm.

I’ll then give a concise, prioritized list of 5–7 firms to call plus a suggested first call order and what to expect from each type.
